concepts.label: Partitioned indexes (Sync Gateway)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - sharding a Sync Gateway GSI index across multiple Couchbase Server index nodes. NOT merged with the promoted fts:index-partitioning (Search Service index partitioning): same word, but a different underlying index kind (Sync Gateway's own allDocs/channels GSI indexes vs Search full-text indexes) and a different service (Index Service vs Search Service). No page states the two are the same mechanism, so kept apart per the standing no-silent-merge rule - flagged for reconciliation as a same-name/different-referent pair worth checking.

relations.subject: sgw:index-partitioning
relations.evidence: Partitioned indexes are an optimization in Sync Gateway intended only for deployments using Memory-Optimized Indexes (MOI) on Couchbase Server, and only when those MOI indexes have grown too large to fit on a single index node.

relations.subject: sgw:index-partitioning
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted tradesOffAgainst, SYMMETRIC) - partitioning is itself a performance cost paid to keep MOI indexes usable
relations.evidence: This can decrease performance, as each partition is queried separately and results are aggregated.

relations.subject: sgw:index-init-endpoint
relations.evidence: Run [POST /{db}/\_index\_init](../rest-api/rest%5Fapi%5Fadmin.md#tag/Database-Management/operation/post%5Fdb-%5Findex%5Finit) on the new instance with `num_partitions` set to the required number of partitions.

relations.subject: sgw:post-upgrade-endpoint
relations.evidence: Manually delete old Sync Gateway indexes.

relations.subject: sgw:configuration-group
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted hasExecutionConstraint) - calling this endpoint under a misaligned configuration group is a documented hazard, not a normal operating mode
relations.evidence: If you are using [configuration groups](../configuration/configuration-overview.md#lbl-config-grp) running on a different index configuration, calling [POST /\_post\_upgrade](../rest-api/rest%5Fapi%5Fadmin.md#tag/Server/operation/post%5F%5Fpost%5Fupgrade) can delete indexes out from under a running database.

relations.subject: sgw:configuration-group
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (promoted cascadesTo) - a misaligned config-group post-upgrade deletes active indexes, which on Server 7.6+ causes a fall-through to sequential scan
relations.evidence: Misalignment between config groups can lead to unexpected deletion of active indexes if [POST /\_post\_upgrade](../rest-api/rest%5Fapi%5Fadmin.md#tag/Server/operation/post%5F%5Fpost%5Fupgrade) is run. This will result in:

notable_absence.finding: The page's only access-control guidance for this destructive, hard-to-reverse operation ('Indexes are not deletable from Couchbase Server once creation starts. Reverting requires downtime and manual deletion.') is informal: 'Make sure only advanced users (typically Architects or Admins) modify partitioning settings.' No Sync Gateway or Server RBAC role, permission, or Admin-API-scoped restriction is named - unlike comparable high-risk operations elsewhere in the registry that are gated by a stated requiresRole/requiresPrivilege relation. This mirrors deployment.md's identical pattern for import-node cardinality (also this batch): a hazard the docs manage through prose discouragement rather than an enforced product guardrail.

cross_component_finding: This page's own Guardrails section proposes, rather than states as existing, product-level protection: 'Optionally set feature flags or config validation, if available, to restrict low-risk deployments from using this feature' - conditional wording ('if available') suggesting even the DOCUMENTATION is unsure whether such a guardrail exists in the product today. Recorded as a finding rather than a relation because it describes an aspiration, not a stated capability.
cross_product_finding: index:sequential-scan (minted and promoted from the Couchbase Server Query-service reference tree) reappears here as the concrete, named consequence of a Sync Gateway operational mistake - a genuine cross-product causal chain (Sync Gateway config-group misalignment -> Server index deletion -> Server Query-service degraded fallback) traceable through a single promoted concept.
